newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich mounts blistering attack on Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich mounts blistering attack on Clinton.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich harshly attacked President Bill Clinton on Saturday, accusing him of soliciting illicit campaign funds from foreigners, harbouring "addicts" in the White House and opening U.S. borders to illegal immigrants with AIDS.

In a campaign speech to the Republican Party faithful in his home district, Gingrich charged Clinton with lying on a range of issues from drugs to Medicare and suggested the White House compromised its China policy to raise election funds from Asian nationals.

The Georgia Republican also revived his claim that drug-users make up one-quarter of the White House staff, saying Clinton chose to shut an on-site FBI liaison office rather than expose guilty staff members.

"On Inauguration Day, they're breaking the law and doing drugs. Two days later, they're in the White House. This must be the most disciplined set of addicts in the world, because none of them has ever used drugs once since they joined the White House staff," Gingrich quipped to an audience at a restaurant in this Atlanta suburb.

"When the FBI reported to the president that he had drug users on his staff, they closed the FBI office ... Their answer wasn't to get rid of the drug users, it was to get rid of the police. And you want to know how liberal they are?"

Gingrich's charges were the most damning against the president since earlier in this election year, when Republicans accused the administration of deliberately using the FBI to obtain files on leading party officials.
The attack also came at a time when some Republicans have criticised presidential candidate Bob Dole for failing to take a hard line against Clinton on the character issue.
After his speech, Gingrich spoke by telephone to Dole, who is considering stepping up attacks on Clinton."
Gingrich is running for re-election against Democrat Michael Coles, a millionaire cookie magnate.

Noting an article in Saturday's Washington Post about a $425,000 Democratic campaign contribution from an Indonesian couple, Gingrich seized his chance to cast the president as the central figure in a political scandal of "historic proportions."
"This is the undermining of the American constitutional process by foreign money illegally penetrating our system," Gingrich told his overwhelmingly conservative audience.

The Post said the couple gave the money to the Democratic National Committee (DNC) after meeting with a Commerce Department official who has since joined the DNC. The U.S. official once worked for an Indonesian conglomerate, in which one of the couple's relatives owns a major stake.
Saying the White House organised a $1 billion sale to China for the same Indonesian company, Gingrich tried to impugn the credibility of White House foreign policy.
"(The administration) probably had its human rights policy towards China influenced by this Indonesian," he proposed.

"The president has been soliciting money from foreign nationals? The greatest power in the world being rented to foreigners? This is a scandal that has historic implications. It makes Watergate look trivial."

Gingrich also said the White House stopped Republican leaders in Congress this year from closing "loopholes for illegal immigrants" contained in the welfare reform bill that Clinton has signed into law.

"Under the Clinton admininstration, you can come to America illegally -- sneak into the country -- announce that you are HIV positive, be declared a political refugee, be eligible for $120,000 of health benefits," he said.

"When the word gets out across the planet, sneak into America and get health care for free, how many people are going to try to get in? By how much are they going to increase illegal immigration by creating this brand-new welfare program?"
